automotive-ev-battery.title: Tesla offers severance packages to striking workers in Sweden
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Tesla has resolved a nearly three-year labor dispute with Swedish trade union IF Metall by settling with all striking union members through severance packages. The resolution marks a significant conclusion to one of the longest-running labor conflicts involving the automaker in Europe.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Porsche Ditches Volkswagen Group Emissions Pool, Joins Up With XPENG
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Porsche has withdrawn from the Volkswagen Group's emissions compliance pool and partnered with Chinese automaker XPENG to meet European Union CO2 reduction requirements. This strategic shift reflects changing dynamics in the global automotive industry's approach to emissions regulations and international collaboration.

automotive-ev-battery.title: VinFast's Vietnam Sales Surge as EVs Enter a Tipping Point
automotive-ev-battery.summary: VinFast delivered 21,781 electric vehicles in Vietnam during July, bringing its seven-month total to 137,697 units and demonstrating a 21.3 percent month-over-month sales increase. The company is on track to substantially exceed its previous annual sales record in its home market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: China Exports 1 Million Automobiles in a Month … Twice
automotive-ev-battery.summary: China has achieved a significant export milestone by shipping over one million vehicles in a single month, with electric vehicles playing a major role in this achievement. The milestone underscores China's dominant position in global automotive manufacturing and EV market expansion.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Porsche reportedly plans to discontinue Taycan by 2030
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Porsche plans to discontinue the Taycan electric sports car by 2030 at the latest, following a sharp decline in sales after strong initial demand since the model's 2019 launch. The company has also reportedly abandoned plans to relocate production from Stuttgart to Leipzig.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Pony.ai and Uber plan over 2,000 robotaxis in Europe
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Pony.ai and Uber plan to expand their autonomous vehicle operations across Europe with a target fleet of more than 2,000 robotaxis, launching services in four additional European cities alongside Zagreb. This expansion represents a significant investment in autonomous mobility services on the continent.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Turning millions of Teslas and Mach-Es into V2L power stations: WETOX D2 earns world's first Next-Gen V2X certification from SGS
automotive-ev-battery.summary: WETOX has received the world's first Next-Generation V2X certification for its D2 power adapter, which enables vehicle-to-load capability on millions of existing Tesla and Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles previously sold without native V2L functionality. The adapter allows owners to tap into their vehicle's battery to power tools, appliances, and emergency home loads.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Gas Stations are Changing Globally. How Has It Changed in Your Town? (Part 2: Europe)
automotive-ev-battery.summary: BP Pulse has invested 100 million dollars in Tesla Supercharger hardware and deployed specialized adapters at its retail sites to support both North American Charging Standard and Combined Charging System standards. This development reflects the broader transformation of legacy gas station networks into EV charging infrastructure across Europe.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Prague extends streetlight charging project until 2028
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Prague is continuing its modernization of street lighting infrastructure to support electric mobility by preparing selected lamp posts for future EV charging points. The project timeline has been extended from the original 2026 completion date to 2028.

automotive-ev-battery.title: France introduces incentive scheme for used EVs
automotive-ev-battery.summary: France has introduced a financial incentive program beginning in September to support the purchase and leasing of used electric vehicles, offering approximately 337 euros per vehicle through the CEE system, with enhanced subsidies available for healthcare workers. The measure represents an effort to accelerate used EV adoption among cost-conscious consumers.

world-news.title: Iran war live: Talks on Hormuz Strait continue; Israel kills 11 in Lebanon
world-news.summary: Israel has conducted its deadliest attacks on Lebanon since a June truce, killing 11 people in strikes on Hezbollah positions, while Iran and Oman continue diplomatic negotiations regarding the strategic Hormuz Strait. The escalation marks a significant development in regional tensions amid ongoing US-Iran conflict dynamics.

world-news.title: Why is the latest Ebola outbreak worsening?
world-news.summary: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than containment efforts can manage, representing a significant public health crisis with global pandemic implications. The deteriorating situation underscores challenges in disease surveillance and response capacity in the region.

world-news.title: Rescuers search for survivors of powerful Indonesia earthquake
world-news.summary: A major earthquake in Indonesia has killed at least 47 people and destroyed hundreds of buildings, with ongoing rescue operations and damage assessments underway. The disaster has significant humanitarian and economic implications for the region.

world-news.title: Colombia asks Trump to suspend tariffs as country reels from earthquake
world-news.summary: Colombia has requested the United States suspend recently imposed tariffs as the nation faces earthquake recovery costs estimated at $6.4 billion. The request highlights tensions between US trade policy and humanitarian concerns in the aftermath of natural disaster.

world-news.title: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
world-news.summary: Qatar has denied Iranian claims that it is holding three Iranian military pilots shot down at the beginning of the US-Iran war. The dispute centers on whether Qatar is detaining the pilots or if Iran's assertion is part of broader geopolitical tensions.

world-news.title: Yemen's government says Houthi strikes hit residential areas in Marib
world-news.summary: Yemen's Ministry of Information has condemned Houthi attacks on the Marib region as an escalation that threatens civilian lives and increases humanitarian suffering. The strikes represent a continuation of the ongoing Yemen conflict with significant civilian impact.

world-news.title: Canadian petition to expel US ambassador gains over 170,000 signatures
world-news.summary: A Canadian petition calling for the expulsion of the US ambassador has exceeded 170,000 signatures and will be discussed by Parliament, reflecting growing discontent with Trump administration policies. The development signals significant diplomatic tension between Canada and the United States.

world-news.title: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to cross into Ceuta, reports say
world-news.summary: Moroccan security forces have apprehended dozens of migrants attempting to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta following intelligence of planned mass crossings. The operation reflects ongoing migration pressures at the North Africa-Europe border.

world-news.title: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, authorities say
world-news.summary: Israel's military has conducted strikes on southern Lebanon targeting what it describes as Hezbollah infrastructure, resulting in eleven deaths according to Lebanese authorities. The strikes represent a significant escalation in Israel-Hezbollah tensions.

world-news.title: US Democrats finalise major shakeup to 2028 presidential primary calendar
world-news.summary: The Democratic Party has restructured its 2028 presidential primary calendar, reinstating South Carolina as the first nominating contest and removing Iowa from its traditional leading position. The change represents a significant shift in the US electoral process with implications for campaign strategy.

tech-ai.title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude's new watermarks will work
tech-ai.summary: Anthropic has unveiled additional technical specifications regarding Claude's watermarking system, addressing key questions about implementation and effectiveness. The details clarify how watermarks function, their resistance to editing attempts, and implications for code generation across the platform.

tech-ai.title: Vulnerability giving attackers full control of Macs is under active exploitation
tech-ai.summary: A critical security vulnerability in macOS is being actively exploited in the wild, allowing remote attackers to gain unauthorized access without requiring a password through screen-sharing functions. Apple users are advised to apply patches immediately to mitigate the risk of full system compromise.

tech-ai.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
tech-ai.summary: SpaceX has completed its acquisition of Cursor, the AI-powered coding startup, integrating it into the aerospace company's operations. The deal represents SpaceX's expansion into artificial intelligence development tools for software engineering.

tech-ai.title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
tech-ai.summary: A woman has alleged that her stepfather utilized Grok AI technology to convert innocuous childhood photographs into sexually explicit content, highlighting significant safety concerns regarding AI misuse. The incident underscores ongoing challenges in preventing generative AI tools from being weaponized to create child sexual abuse material.

tech-ai.title: How to tell if your AI platforms' accounts have been hacked
tech-ai.summary: TechCrunch has published a comprehensive guide to help users identify unauthorized access to their accounts on major AI platforms. The resource provides practical steps for detecting compromised credentials and securing accounts across leading AI services.

tech-ai.title: First test flight of largest all-electric aircraft used just $5 of electricity
tech-ai.summary: A major milestone in aviation technology was achieved as the largest all-electric aircraft completed its inaugural test flight with remarkably low energy costs. An airline-backed venture is advancing its hybrid-electric commercial aircraft program with the goal of revolutionizing sustainable aviation.

tech-ai.title: Every fusion startup that has raised over $100M
tech-ai.summary: A new analysis reveals that fusion energy startups have collectively raised $7.1 billion in funding, with the majority concentrated among a select group of well-capitalized companies. The data provides a comprehensive overview of the investment landscape in nuclear fusion technology development.

tech-ai.title: So much solar: Digging into the list of every US power plant that went online this year
tech-ai.summary: Utility-scale solar capacity dominated new US power plant installations this year, with battery storage systems following as the second-leading source of new generation capacity. The data demonstrates a substantial continued shift away from fossil fuel-based energy infrastructure.

tech-ai.title: Xteink's tiny e-readers are getting access to free books through Libby
tech-ai.summary: Xteink e-reader devices now support access to free DRM-protected ebooks through Libby via new CrossPoint Reader plugin functionality. The development significantly improves the digital library accessibility for users of budget-friendly Xteink e-readers, addressing a previous limitation compared to established competitors.

tech-ai.title: We're reaching peak camera with the Sony A7R VI
tech-ai.summary: Sony's latest flagship A7R VI camera delivers a 66.8-megapixel sensor with significant performance improvements in resolution, speed, and videography capabilities without sacrificing usability across diverse shooting scenarios. The advancement represents a major evolution in high-resolution camera technology with substantially improved versatility.

science-space.title: A stress hormone may help the brain repair itself
science-space.summary: Researchers have discovered that the stress hormone CRH is rapidly released by myelin-producing precursor cells near damaged brain tissue, facilitating the repair of protective nerve insulation. This mechanism also influences brain development and myelin thickness, potentially offering insights into how early-life stress contributes to psychiatric disorders.

science-space.title: Scientists detect a surprising shift in human blood as CO2 rises
science-space.summary: A comprehensive analysis of over two decades of U.S. health data reveals that rising atmospheric carbon dioxide has produced measurable changes in human blood composition, with bicarbonate levels increasing approximately 7% since 1999 while calcium and phosphorus have declined. These biochemical shifts closely correlate with increases in atmospheric CO2 concentrations.

science-space.title: When gut microbes run low on fiber, they may start eating you
science-space.summary: New research demonstrates that when dietary fiber is insufficient, gut microbes may consume proteins from the protective mucus lining of the intestines. The study found that adequate fiber intake suppresses this process, while indigestible plant proteins promote the production of beneficial microbial compounds.

science-space.title: A Sunflower's View of Totality
science-space.summary: NASA captured striking imagery of a total solar eclipse as the Moon passed between the Sun and Earth, producing a spectacular celestial event visible from Spain in August 2026. The unique perspective documents this significant astronomical phenomenon from an Earth-based vantage point.

science-space.title: APOD: 2026 August 14 – Total Solar Eclipse from Greenland
science-space.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day features imagery and scientific analysis of a total solar eclipse visible from Greenland in August 2026. The featured image provides professional astronomical context for this major celestial event.

science-space.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 223 — The Lunar Domain
science-space.summary: In Episode 223 of This Week In Space, hosts Rod Pyle and Dale Skran discuss the future of lunar exploration with Dr. Scott Pace, examining policy and scientific priorities for sustained Moon missions. The episode addresses key considerations shaping humanity's next phase of lunar activities.

science-space.title: On this day in space! Aug. 15, 1977: Mysterious 'Wow!' Signal boosts search for E.T.
science-space.summary: On August 15, 1977, astronomers detected the now-famous 'Wow!' signal using Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope, a mysterious narrowband radio transmission that remains unexplained nearly 50 years later. The signal remains one of the most intriguing candidates in the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

science-space.title: APOD: 2026 August 15 – Bright Perseids from Sweden
science-space.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights stunning observations of the Perseid meteor shower as captured from Sweden in August 2026. The featured image showcases this annual celestial event with professional astronomical analysis.

science-space.title: 'Strap yourself in and feel the Gs': NASA announces 'Max Power' aerospace expo
science-space.summary: NASA announced a two-day aerospace exposition scheduled for November 2026, featuring hands-on demonstrations and exhibits related to aerospace engineering and space exploration. The event aims to engage public interest in NASA's current and future missions and technological innovations.

science-space.title: Author Correction: Cretaceous bird from Brazil informs the evolution of the avian skull and brain
science-space.summary: This article presents a correction to a previously published study examining fossil evidence from a Cretaceous bird specimen discovered in Brazil. The research provides important insights into the evolutionary development of avian cranial and neurological structures.

finance-markets.title: OpenAI upheaval mounts as Sam Altman readies IPO push
finance-markets.summary: OpenAI is preparing for a major initial public offering as executive departures and changes to its safety team create internal uncertainty. The company's market valuation and governance structure are likely to face significant scrutiny from investors and regulators as it transitions to public markets.

finance-markets.title: Bond Traders Agonize Over AI Companies' $70 Billion of Shadow Credit Backstops
finance-markets.summary: Major AI companies including Nvidia have accumulated approximately $70 billion in off-balance-sheet liabilities through financing arrangements that do not appear on their financial statements. Bond traders are concerned these phantom liabilities could materialize unexpectedly during market stress, creating systemic risk in credit markets.

finance-markets.title: Traders are spoiling for a fight over the yen
finance-markets.summary: Currency traders are positioning for increased volatility in the yen following coordinated US-Japan intervention in foreign exchange markets. The market tensions suggest elevated risks of sudden currency movements and potential central bank responses that could roil global financial markets.

finance-markets.title: Bally's Warns of Debt Covenant Breach Risk as It Seeks New Funds
finance-markets.summary: Bally's Corp. disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue operating as a going concern due to potential covenant violations with its lenders. The casino operator is actively seeking additional financing to address liquidity pressures and avoid default on its debt obligations.

finance-markets.title: Strong Earnings Keep PNC's Agati Bullish on Stocks
finance-markets.summary: PNC Financial Services' Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati maintains a positive outlook on US equities supported by robust corporate earnings and solid economic fundamentals. However, she acknowledges that elevated Treasury yields and midterm political uncertainty could increase market volatility going forward.

finance-markets.title: Peru's Economy Unexpectedly Slows as Fishing, Agriculture Slump
finance-markets.summary: Peru's economic growth slowed unexpectedly in June as adverse weather conditions hampered output in the critical fishing and agriculture sectors. The slowdown raises concerns about the country's growth prospects and inflation control amid external commodity price pressures.

finance-markets.title: China poised to lift travel ban on Manus founders
finance-markets.summary: China is expected to lift restrictions on the travel of Manus AI company founders, including Chief Executive Xiao Hong, as the company nears resolution of its separation from Meta. The development signals potential resolution of regulatory tensions between Beijing and the AI venture.

finance-markets.title: Lakers Deal Caps Billionaire Rush Into Sports
finance-markets.summary: Bob Iger and Josh Kushner have agreed to purchase the Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5 billion, capping a broader wave of billionaire investment in professional sports franchises. The transaction comes as other major deals reshape ownership in the NBA and other sports properties, signaling the attractiveness of sports assets to ultra-wealthy investors.

finance-markets.title: AI vs the people
finance-markets.summary: Author Jill Lepore examines how opposition to large data centres is reshaping political landscapes, drawing historical parallels to regulatory challenges faced by transformative technologies. The analysis suggests that political resistance to AI infrastructure development could significantly impact the industry's expansion trajectory.

finance-markets.title: Colombia Quake Tests New President Days Into Term
finance-markets.summary: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake in western Colombia has killed at least 287 people and disrupted coffee exports during the first days of President Abelardo de la Espriella's administration. The natural disaster presents an immediate crisis management test for the new government and threatens to disrupt global coffee supplies.

startups-vc.title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
startups-vc.summary: Cognition, an AI coding startup, is reportedly in early-stage discussions to raise capital at a $40 billion valuation, just months after closing a $1 billion funding round at a $26 billion valuation. The potential raise would represent a significant 54% increase in the company's valuation in a short timeframe, underscoring investor appetite for high-performing AI development tools.

startups-vc.title: Lovable confirms new $13.3B valuation, raises another $400M
startups-vc.summary: Lovable, an AI web development platform, has secured $400 million in new funding at a $13.3 billion valuation following strong commercial momentum. The funding round comes after the company achieved $500 million in annualized run rate revenue in June, demonstrating significant traction in the AI-powered developer tools market.

startups-vc.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
startups-vc.summary: SpaceX has officially completed its acquisition of Cursor, an AI-powered coding assistant, integrating the startup into the aerospace company's operations. The acquisition underscores SpaceX's strategic interest in AI development tools to enhance its engineering capabilities.

startups-vc.title: Every fusion startup that has raised over $100M
startups-vc.summary: Fusion energy startups have collectively raised $7.1 billion to date, with the majority of capital concentrated among a select few well-funded companies. The funding landscape reveals significant investor confidence in fusion technology as a long-term solution for clean energy production.

startups-vc.title: Meesho Goes Public
startups-vc.summary: Meesho, a Y Combinator S16 alumnus, has completed its initial public offering, becoming one of India's largest e-commerce platforms that empowers small merchants. The IPO milestone represents a decade of growth from startup to public company for founders Vidit and Sanjeev.

startups-vc.title: Exclusive: ClearJet raises $25M to build the 'Uber of Cargo'
startups-vc.summary: ClearJet, an AI-enabled logistics platform that connects shippers with unused cargo capacity on commercial flights, has raised $25 million in Series B funding led by Edison Partners. The Austin-based startup is positioned to disrupt the cargo logistics industry through technology-driven capacity optimization.

startups-vc.title: Sector Snapshot: Fitness Startup Funding Is Rebounding, But Investors Want AI And Data, Not Treadmills
startups-vc.summary: Venture funding for fitness and wellness startups exceeded $3.6 billion in the first half of 2026, with investor enthusiasm focused on AI-powered and data-driven solutions rather than hardware. The sector is on track to grow approximately one-third compared to 2025, signaling renewed investor confidence.

startups-vc.title: How a $250 million acquisition collapsed into allegations of fraud and forged signatures
startups-vc.summary: A $250 million acquisition involving VideoVerse has unraveled amid serious allegations of fraud and forged signatures, leaving investors awaiting their share of proceeds and creating multiple legal cases. Co-founder Vinayak Shrivastav is at the center of the ongoing legal disputes.

startups-vc.title: Christopher Golda and Grey Baker Join YC as General Partners
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator has announced the appointment of Christopher Golda and Grey Baker as General Partners, expanding the accelerator's investment and mentorship capabilities. The additions strengthen YC's leadership team and ability to support its portfolio companies.

startups-vc.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
startups-vc.summary: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based technology companies were affected by mass layoffs in 2025, with workforce reductions continuing into 2026. The tracker provides ongoing visibility into major tech sector job cuts across the industry.

crypto-web3.title: OCC grants conditional approval for Trump-backed World Liberty National Trust bank
crypto-web3.summary: President Donald Trump-backed World Liberty Financial has secured preliminary approval to become a national trust bank, a significant regulatory milestone for the firm. This approval enables the entity to pursue stablecoin issuance and expand its footprint in regulated crypto banking services.

crypto-web3.title: Trump, CFTC Chair Selig expected at Wednesday White House meeting with crypto and prediction market executives
crypto-web3.summary: A high-level White House meeting between President Trump, CFTC Chair Selig, and crypto and prediction market executives is scheduled to kick off the CFTC's first Innovation Advisory Committee meeting. The session signals heightened regulatory engagement and potential policy direction for the digital assets sector.

crypto-web3.title: The $11.2 billion in 2026 funding that killed crypto's permissionless era
crypto-web3.summary: Major institutional investors including BlackRock and Goldman Sachs have concentrated funding into regulated crypto firms in the first half of 2026, marking a structural shift toward centralized, compliant platforms. This trend reflects Wall Street's preference for regulatory clarity and institutional-grade infrastructure over decentralized alternatives.

crypto-web3.title: Swiss mega-bank UBS ramps up its Bitcoin exposure with a massive 24-fold surge in ETF call options
crypto-web3.summary: UBS significantly increased its Bitcoin exposure through a 24-fold surge in BlackRock Bitcoin ETF call options while also raising direct IBIT holdings by 12 percent during the quarter. The move reflects major institutional confidence in Bitcoin's asset class maturation and long-term value proposition.

crypto-web3.title: Israel's largest bank taps Galaxy to offer bitcoin, ether and solana trading
crypto-web3.summary: Israel's leading financial institution has partnered with Galaxy Digital to offer cryptocurrency trading services for major digital assets including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana. The initiative reflects growing institutional adoption of crypto services in the region, which saw significant onchain activity totaling $22 billion in the prior 12 months.

crypto-web3.title: Paul Tudor Jones' investment firm increases stake in BlackRock's bitcoin ETF after year of selling
crypto-web3.summary: Paul Tudor Jones' investment firm has reversed its prior divestment trend by increasing its position in BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF following a year of net selling activity. The shift signals renewed confidence from a major hedge fund operator in Bitcoin's long-term institutional viability.

crypto-web3.title: French tax breach exposes nearly 678,000 people as crypto wrench attacks pile up
crypto-web3.summary: A significant data breach exposing personal and financial records of approximately 678,000 French taxpayers and businesses has surfaced, coinciding with a surge in violent wrench attacks targeting cryptocurrency holders. France is on pace for its worst year on record for crypto-related physical security incidents.

crypto-web3.title: Wall Street's private blockchain obsession is a 'race to the bottom,' Ethereum advocate Raman warns
crypto-web3.summary: Ethereum advocates caution that Wall Street's focus on centralized, permission-based blockchain networks undermines the core benefits of blockchain technology without proper transparency and openness. The criticism highlights the philosophical divide between traditional finance's infrastructure preferences and decentralized blockchain principles.

crypto-web3.title: JPMorgan cut Polymarket's banking ties in October but still wants a role in a potential IPO
crypto-web3.summary: JPMorgan severed banking relationships with prediction market platform Polymarket in October but reportedly remains interested in participating in the company's potential future initial public offering. Polymarket has transitioned to an undisclosed alternative lender while maintaining active discussions with JPMorgan.

crypto-web3.title: Why the world's second-largest Bitcoin mining power is shutting down rigs in its capital city
crypto-web3.summary: A major Bitcoin mining jurisdiction has enacted year-round restrictions requiring operators to shut down mining rigs in its capital city to address power capacity shortages and grid strain. The regulatory action reflects growing tension between energy-intensive crypto mining operations and regional infrastructure limitations.

cybersecurity.title: Lazarus Exploits Windows Zero-Day to Gain SYSTEM Access and Deploy Backdoor
cybersecurity.summary: The North Korean-linked Lazarus Group has exploited a newly patched Windows zero-day vulnerability to deliver a previously unknown backdoor targeting defense and aerospace companies across France, Germany, Brazil, and India. The exploitation is part of Operation Dream Job, a long-running cyber espionage campaign attributed to the threat actor.

cybersecurity.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
cybersecurity.summary: A 26-year-old Canadian man identified as a major 2024 cybercrime threat actor has pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy for hacking and extorting more than 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage service. The defendant also admitted to stealing call and text history records from more than 100 million AT&T customers.

cybersecurity.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code
cybersecurity.summary: SAP has released patches for a maximum-severity vulnerability in Commerce Cloud (Data Hub Adapter) rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. The flaw stems from insufficient authorization checks and input validation in the affected system.

cybersecurity.title: Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws
cybersecurity.summary: Adobe has released security updates addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities in ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic, including three flaws with perfect CVSS 10.0 scores that could enable arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation. The patches address operating system command injection and other severe security gaps.

cybersecurity.title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
cybersecurity.summary: Two malicious LiteLLM releases containing credential-stealing code were distributed on PyPI for approximately 40 minutes in March, potentially exposing over 2,100 organizations. The compromised packages were capable of harvesting cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, database passwords, and other sensitive secrets from systems.

cybersecurity.title: Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access
cybersecurity.summary: Threat actors have begun actively exploiting CVE-2026-59310, a critical directory-traversal vulnerability in Broadcom VMware vCenter rated 9.8 on the CVSS scale, to achieve arbitrary code execution and persistent remote access. The vulnerability affects vCenter servers and can be exploited by attackers with network access to the affected systems.

cybersecurity.title: 737 Chrome VPN Extensions Caught Routing Traffic Through Proxies
cybersecurity.summary: Security researchers have identified 737 malicious free VPN and proxy extensions in the Chrome Web Store targeting primarily Russian-speaking users, collectively downloaded over 75,000 times. These extensions intercept browser traffic and route it through attacker-controlled proxy infrastructure, exposing users' sensitive communications and data.

cybersecurity.title: Lessons Learned from CISA's Recent GitHub Leak
cybersecurity.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has published a postmortem on a significant data leak where a contractor exposed dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS Govcloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident and response provide critical lessons for security teams on credential management and breach notification procedures.

cybersecurity.title: LG to Ban Residential Proxies from Smart TV Apps
cybersecurity.summary: LG Electronics USA announced plans to suspend apps from its webOS smart TV store that convert televisions into always-on residential proxy nodes, following research showing over 42 percent of games and apps in the store enable unauthorized third-party Internet traffic routing. The action addresses privacy and security concerns from users whose devices are being exploited for proxy services.

cybersecurity.title: Who's Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
cybersecurity.summary: A new free service called DecryptAds aggregates and analyzes advertising technology data to help users identify which entities are tracking them across websites and mobile applications. The tool makes previously semi-public but difficult-to-access adtech information transparent and easily searchable for individual users.

health-biotech.title: FDA approves Bristol multiple myeloma treatment, marking debut of novel drug class
health-biotech.summary: The FDA has approved Zenbexus, a Bristol Myers Squibb treatment for advanced multiple myeloma, representing the first approval in a new class of protein-degrading CELMoD medicines. This milestone approval could help Bristol Myers strengthen a key drug franchise acquired from Celgene and addresses an important unmet need in blood cancer treatment.

health-biotech.title: STAT+: Epic's alleged anticompetitive practices under scrutiny from federal, state investigators
health-biotech.summary: Epic Systems, a dominant healthcare software vendor, is facing a broad inquiry from FTC investigators into its business practices, according to sources contacted during the investigation. The scrutiny represents a significant antitrust action against one of the healthcare industry's most influential technology companies.

health-biotech.title: Psychedelics developer Definium scores more positive data for LSD pill
health-biotech.summary: Definium Technologies reported positive late-stage trial results for its LSD-based treatment for generalized anxiety disorder, with analysts characterizing the data as a decisive victory. The findings position the psychedelic medicine as a potential multibillion-dollar opportunity in the emerging field of psychiatric therapeutics.

health-biotech.title: Lilly files six lawsuits in bid to shut down 'black market' for retatrutide
health-biotech.summary: Eli Lilly has filed multiple lawsuits against unauthorized sellers offering versions of retatrutide, its anticipated weight-loss medicine, ahead of formal regulatory approval. The action underscores the intense market demand for the triple-hormone agonist and the company's efforts to protect intellectual property and ensure drug safety.

health-biotech.title: PTC takes a chance on Sangamo's Fabry disease gene therapy
health-biotech.summary: PTC Therapeutics has entered a high-risk, high-reward agreement regarding Sangamo Biotherapies' Fabry disease gene therapy, which is approaching regulatory approval. Wall Street analysts view the deal as a bet on a treatment that could potentially outperform existing therapeutic options in this rare genetic disorder.

health-biotech.title: New Taiho, Cullinan data heats up lung cancer drug battle
health-biotech.summary: Taiho and Cullinan's zipalertinib generated trial data positioning it as a competitive threat to multiple approved lung cancer therapies while establishing a clinical benchmark for similar drugs in development. The results indicate the drug's potential to significantly impact treatment options for advanced non-small cell lung cancer.

health-biotech.title: Capricor shares spike on CEO comments; Cytokinetics sues Bristol Myers
health-biotech.summary: Capricor Therapeutics' stock surged after the CEO indicated the FDA is open to reviewing an updated submission for its Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy, while separately, Cytokinetics initiated legal action against Bristol Myers in a competitive dispute over a heart failure drug. The developments highlight ongoing regulatory dynamics and litigation in the biotech sector.

health-biotech.title: STAT+: PBMs agree to display TrumpRx drug prices
health-biotech.summary: Pharmacy Benefit Managers have agreed to display drug prices under a TrumpRx initiative, while Bristol's Zenbexus won accelerated approval and Novartis secured a UK patent victory for Entresto. These developments reflect regulatory and competitive shifts in pharmaceutical pricing and intellectual property enforcement.

health-biotech.title: Bristol Myers wins 'milestone' FDA approval of myeloma drug acquired from Celgene
health-biotech.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb obtained FDA approval for Zenbexus, representing a significant milestone as the first CELMoD protein-degrading medicine approved for multiple myeloma. The clearance marks an important step in Bristol's strategy to revitalize drug franchises acquired from its Celgene acquisition.

health-biotech.title: Biotech initiatives pick up as more regions race to become hubs
health-biotech.summary: Multiple U.S. regions, including Pennsylvania and Kansas City, are intensifying efforts to establish themselves as biotech hubs through increased government funding and infrastructure investments. Industry experts caution that financial investment alone will not determine where pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies ultimately build their operations.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What is in China's new five-year plan for climate change?
energy-climate.summary: China has released its 15th five-year plan dedicated to addressing climate change, outlining the country's climate strategy and commitments. The plan is significant given China's status as the world's largest emitter and its critical role in global climate negotiations.

energy-climate.title: Texas hits new peak demand record, but supply constraints will limit growth
energy-climate.summary: Texas set a new peak electricity demand record, but analysis shows that more than 80 percent of new large industrial loads seeking interconnection will lack matching generation online by 2030, creating significant supply constraints. The challenge is exacerbated by surging demand from data centers and industrial facilities.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: Weaker EV targets could cost UK consumers £3bn a year by 2030
energy-climate.summary: Analysis shows that a UK government consultation to weaken electric vehicle targets could cost consumers approximately £3 billion annually by 2030. The proposed policy change would delay the transition to EVs and increase consumer energy costs.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: Does the world need 'carbon capture and storage' to reach net-zero?
energy-climate.summary: This analysis examines whether carbon capture and storage technology is essential for achieving global net-zero emissions targets. The article explores the role of CCS in climate mitigation strategies and its feasibility at scale.

energy-climate.title: PJM eyes data center, crypto reliability requirements after 3.8 GW of load trips offline
energy-climate.summary: PJM Interconnection is considering implementing ride-through standards for data centers following a major outage in Northern Virginia where 3.8 GW of data center and cryptocurrency mining loads tripped offline. The incident highlights grid stability concerns amid rapidly growing data center demand.

energy-climate.title: Record-setting geothermal bid signals rising interest in federal leases
energy-climate.summary: A federal geothermal lease parcel in New Mexico sold for a record $701 per acre in June, signaling increased competition and investor interest in geothermal energy development. The Bureau of Land Management is preparing additional lease sales, with another scheduled for August 18 in Utah.

energy-climate.title: Cadeler signs $929m contract for T-class wind installation vessels
energy-climate.summary: Cadeler has secured firm contracts valued at approximately $929 million with COSCO Shipping Offshore to construct T-class wind installation vessels. The investment reflects growing demand for offshore wind infrastructure and vessel capacity.

energy-climate.title: Software-based initiative could unlock up to 20% more bulk capacity: OATI
energy-climate.summary: OATI is pursuing federal funding for dynamic line rating software, near-real-time inter-regional coordination, and AI-enhanced resource dispatch to unlock up to 20 percent additional bulk transmission capacity without requiring new infrastructure. The approach offers a cost-efficient alternative to physical grid expansion.

energy-climate.title: ConEd plans 28 new substations by 2035
energy-climate.summary: New York-based utility ConEd announced plans to construct 28 new substations by 2035 to support electrification and align with city and state climate policies. The infrastructure investment reflects the company's strategy to enable grid modernization and clean energy adoption.

energy-climate.title: Edify achieves financial close for Ganymirra and Majors Creek projects
energy-climate.summary: Edify Energy has achieved financial close on the Ganymirra and Majors Creek solar and battery hybrid projects located in North Queensland. The projects represent significant investment in renewable energy and energy storage infrastructure in Australia.

asia-pacific.title: Taiwan drone defences fall short against Beijing's evolving technology, audit reveals
asia-pacific.summary: A Taiwan government audit has revealed significant technical shortcomings in the country's counter-drone defense systems, with a major procurement program collapsing after repeated testing failures. The findings underscore growing concerns that Taipei's capabilities are lagging behind Beijing's rapidly advancing drone technology, creating potential security vulnerabilities amid escalating cross-strait tensions.

asia-pacific.title: Australia urged to lead Indo-Pacific cable shield as hybrid war risks rise
asia-pacific.summary: A new report calls for Australia to position itself as an "Indo-Pacific preferred cable hub" to address mounting security and economic risks posed by vulnerability of submarine cables in contested regional waters. Regional analysts support the recommendation that Australia leverage this strategic vulnerability into a competitive advantage amid growing hybrid warfare threats to critical undersea infrastructure.

asia-pacific.title: China's 1MW perovskite solar farm beats silicon system in industrial-scale test
asia-pacific.summary: A China-led research team has achieved a major breakthrough in commercializing perovskite solar technology by developing a super-stable coating suitable for industrial-scale manufacturing of next-generation panels. The advancement clears the final significant technical hurdle toward producing low-cost, high-efficiency solar alternatives to conventional silicon systems.

asia-pacific.title: Indonesia Is the Latest Country to Validate China's Claim to Taiwan – Unwittingly or Not
asia-pacific.summary: Indonesia has become the latest nation to effectively endorse China's increasingly strict interpretation of the One China principle, as Beijing systematically enlists foreign countries across Africa, Oceania, and Southeast Asia to validate its territorial claims. The pattern reflects Beijing's coordinated diplomatic strategy to isolate Taiwan internationally.

asia-pacific.title: Commentary: Japan needs deterrence and renewal - not managed decline
asia-pacific.summary: A Financial Times commentary argues that Japan must fundamentally rethink its post-war role and strategic posture, moving beyond a policy of managed decline toward renewed deterrence capabilities and global engagement. The piece reflects broader regional concerns about Japan's capacity to maintain its position amid shifting geopolitical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific.

asia-pacific.title: Hong Kong's new university town a test of the city's global ambitions
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong's Northern Metropolis University Town project has progressed from planning concept to implementation phase, with the government expanding the development area to over 1,000 hectares and receiving 19 institutional proposals. The initiative represents a significant test of Hong Kong's capacity to maintain its position as a global higher education hub amid evolving geopolitical circumstances.

asia-pacific.title: Hong Kong stages first counterterrorism drill at redeveloped Huanggang crossing
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong authorities conducted their first counterterrorism drill at the revamped Huanggang border crossing, involving approximately 5,000 civil servants from 30 bureaus to test security and crowd management procedures. The exercise tested integrated response capabilities to potential threats and unexpected surges in passenger traffic at the strategically important checkpoint.

asia-pacific.title: How Singapore's Ascott grew from its first serviced residence into a global hospitality business
asia-pacific.summary: Ascott, founded in Singapore in 1984, has expanded to operate more than 1,000 properties worldwide while maintaining its innovation base in its home city. The company's growth trajectory reflects Singapore's enduring strength as a hospitality and business hub within the Asia-Pacific region.

asia-pacific.title: Afghanistan: 5 Years in the Dark
asia-pacific.summary: A report examines Afghanistan's deterioration under Taliban rule over the past five years, documenting how the regime has systematically ordered half the population to "disappear" through restrictions on women's rights and freedoms. The analysis reflects the humanitarian crisis and regional implications of Afghanistan's isolation and institutional collapse.

asia-pacific.title: In Interview, Japarov Says He'd Planned for Tashiev to Be Kyrgyz President Next
asia-pacific.summary: Kyrgyzstan's leader Japarov revealed in an interview that he had previously planned for Tashiev to succeed him as president but changed his mind after concluding Tashiev was "not ready." The disclosure provides insight into internal power dynamics and succession planning within Kyrgyz leadership circles.
